content.text: Amines and amides are nitrogen-containing organic compounds. Amines are derivatives of ammonia with one or more hydrogens replaced by organic groups. Amides contain a nitrogen atom bonded to a carbonyl carbon.

content.title: Amine Classification
content.code:
graph TD
    A[AMINES] --> B[Primary R-NH2]
    A --> C[Secondary R-NH-R]
    A --> D[Tertiary R-NR-R]
    B --> E[Example: Methylamine CH3NH2]
    C --> F[Example: Dimethylamine]
    D --> G[Example: Trimethylamine]
    style A fill:#2563eb,color:#fff

content.text: Amines are weak bases because the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons that can accept a proton. This basicity is important in biological systems, as many neurotransmitters, hormones, and alkaloids contain amine groups.

content.title: Amine Basicity
content.code:
graph LR
    A[Amine R-NH2] --> B[+ H+]
    B --> C[Ammonium Ion R-NH3+]

content.text: Amines are found in many biologically important molecules: amino acids (building blocks of proteins), neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin), hormones (adrenaline), and alkaloids (nicotine, morphine, caffeine).

content.title: Biologically Important Amines
content.code:
graph TD
    A[Amines in Nature] --> B[Amino Acids
NH2-CHR-COOH]
    A --> C[Neurotransmitters
Dopamine Serotonin]
    A --> D[Alkaloids
Nicotine Morphine]
    A --> E[DNA Bases
Adenine Cytosine]
    style A fill:#c4b5fd

content.text: Amides contain a nitrogen atom connected to the carbonyl carbon (R-CONH2). They are formed by the reaction of carboxylic acids with amines or ammonia (amidation), eliminating water. Amides are key structural units in proteins (peptide bonds).

content.title: Amide Formation
content.code:
graph LR
    A[Carboxylic Acid R-COOH] --> B[+ Amine R-NH2]
    B --> C[Amide R-CONH-R + H2O]
    C --> D[Peptide Bond in Proteins]

content.text: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by amide (peptide) bonds. Amino acids contain both amine and carboxylic acid groups. The 20 standard amino acids combine in different sequences to form proteins with diverse functions: enzymes, structural proteins, hormones, and transport molecules.

content.title: Protein Structure Levels
content.code:
graph TD
    A[PROTEIN STRUCTURE] --> B[Primary Amino acid sequence]
    A --> C[Secondary Alpha helices and Beta sheets]
    A --> D[Tertiary 3D folding]
    A --> E[Quaternary Multiple chains]
    B --> F[Peptide bonds]
    C --> G[Hydrogen bonds]
    D --> H[Interactions between R groups]
    E --> I[Protein complex]
    style A fill:#2563eb,color:#fff

content.text: Kevlar is a synthetic polymer made from two monomers connected by amide bonds. It gets its extraordinary strength from hydrogen bonds between polymer chains and aromatic stacking interactions. Kevlar is five times stronger than steel by weight and is used in body armor, helmets, and protective gear.

content.title: Kevlar Structure and Uses
content.code:
graph TD
    A[Kevlar Monomers] --> B[1,4-Phenylene-diamine]
    A --> C[Terephthaloyl Chloride]
    B --> D[Amide bonds form]
    C --> D
    D --> E[Strong hydrogen bonds between chains]
    E --> F[Body armor Tires Protective gear]

content.text: Alkaloids are naturally occurring cyclic molecules containing amine functional groups. Examples include: Nicotine (from tobacco), Morphine (from poppies), Codeine (pain relief), and Heroin (acetylated morphine, highly addictive). The plant produces these substances as chemical defenses against pests.

content.title: Common Alkaloids
content.code:
graph LR
    A[Nicotine] --> B[Tobacco]
    C[Morphine] --> D[Poppies]
    E[Codeine] --> F[Cough Suppressant]
    G[Heroin] --> H[Addictive Narcotic]

content.text: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) contains nitrogenous bases (adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine) which are amine-containing compounds. The sequence of these bases encodes genetic information. DNA is a double helix with sugar-phosphate backbones on the outside and hydrogen-bonded base pairs on the inside.

content.title: DNA Double Helix
content.code:
graph LR
    A[DNA] --> B[Two strands]
    B --> C[Hydrogen bonds between bases]
    C --> D[A-T and G-C pairing]
    D --> E[Genetic Code]
    E --> F[Proteins]

content.text:
Amines: - Nitrogen bonded to carbon/hydrogen only - Basic (lone pair on N) - Examples: NH3, CH3NH2

Amides: - Nitrogen bonded to carbonyl carbon (C=O) - Not basic (lone pair is delocalized) - Examples: Proteins, Kevlar
